summary: An announcement of the next Network Working Group meeting, hosted by MIT's Project MAC in Cambridge, Massachusetts. It was planned in three phases, starting with a workshop for system programmers, so most people would only attend one or two parts. Its dates were later changed. It was replaced by RFC 212.

eli5.summary: This is a flyer for a big meeting of the people building the early network. There were three parts, and most guests only needed to come to one or two of them.

subtitle: Three-phase meeting for the Network Working Group

tldr.problem: The Network Working Group needed to coordinate work across many early ARPANET sites and bring people together for hands-on demos and planning.
tldr.mechanism: A three-phase meeting was held at MIT's Project MAC in Cambridge from September 26-30, 1971. The first phase was a systems programmers workshop; the second had topic-specific working groups; the third was a plenary session open to all members.
tldr.outcome: The meeting brought together the early network builders for discussion, demos, and planning the future of the ARPANET.

today: RFC 207 is historic. It was superseded by RFC 212, which covered a later NWG meeting.

sections.title: About the Meeting
sections.content:
RFC 207 is an announcement for the Network Working Group meeting hosted by MIT's Project MAC in Cambridge, Massachusetts. It was scheduled to run from September 26 through September 30, 1971.

The meeting was structured in three phases to allow participants to attend only the parts relevant to their work. Attendees needed to register with Anne Speare at Project MAC.
sections.eli5: An invitation to a big gathering of the people building the network, at MIT. Each person could skip the parts they did not need to hear.

sections.title: The Three Phases
sections.content:
The first phase, Systems Programmers Workshop (September 26-27), was for hands-on work. Programmers were expected to create working demonstrations of their host systems over the network and teach other programmers how to use them. The Dynamic Modeling/Computer Graphics PDP-10 system was made available to assist in building these demonstrations.

The second phase (September 28-29) consisted of topic-specific working groups by invitation, covering network climate research, service centers, the NIC, online cooperation, and planning for the International Computer Communications Conference.

The third phase (September 30) was a plenary session open to all NWG members and visitors, where workshop reports and other network activities were presented.
sections.eli5: First, programmers brought their computers and showed them off. Next, small groups talked about special topics they cared about. Finally, everyone got together to hear what had been discussed.

sections.title: Logistics
sections.content: The Network Steering Committee included S. Crocker, J. Heafner, R. Kahn, J. Melvin, and A. Vezza. Attendees could contact Bob Metcalfe or Bob Kahn at BBN for workshop applications, and Anne Speare at Project MAC for registration and room reservations.
sections.eli5: The organizers arranged rooms and kept track of who was coming.
